Which Article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 141 of the Indian Constitution.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ** Article 141 of the Indian Constitution states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.**
 
• This means that all lower courts, including High Courts, must abide by the decisions and rulings made by the Supreme Court.
 
• The purpose of this article is to ensure consistency and uniformity in the interpretation and application of laws across the country.
 
• It also serves as a check on the power of lower courts, preventing them from making decisions that are contrary to established legal principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 140: ** Parliament may by law make provision for conferring upon the Supreme Court such supplemental powers not inconsistent with any of the provisions of this Constitution as may appear to be necessary or desirable for the purpose of enabling the court more effectively to exercise the jurisdiction conferred upon it by or under this Constitution.
 
• **Article 142**, gives the Supreme Court the power to pass any order necessary for doing complete justice in any case or matter pending before it.
 
• **Article 145,** deals with the rules of the Supreme Court, including the number of judges required to sit for a case and the quorum for meetings.

questions.question: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi started the system of Sijda and Paibos?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghiyas ud din Balban.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The correct answer is option 3, i.e. Ghiyas ud din Balban, who was the ninth Sultan of Delhi and ruled from 1266 to 1287 AD.**
 
• ** Sijda and Paibos were two forms of obeisance** that were introduced by Balban to establish his authority and enhance the status of the Sultanate in the eyes of the people.
 
• Sijda involved prostratin**g oneself before the Sultan** and touching his feet as a sign of submission and respect. P**aibos, on the other hand, required the person to kneel before the Sultan and kiss his feet.**
 
• Balban's strict enforcement of these customs was meant to reinforce the idea of the** Sultan as a divine ruler **and to discourage any challenges to his authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Muhammad Bin Tughlug, the second Sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty**, was known for his eccentricities and mismanagement of the empire.
 
• Nasir u din Muhammad was the third Sultan of the Khilji dynasty and is known for his patronage of scholars and poets.
 
• **Qutb ud-Din Aibak was the founder of the Slave dynasty and the first Muslim ruler of Delhi**.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and his construction of the Qutub Minar.
